channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Cell: COP1 is a temperature-responsive switch in Arabidopsis
item.description: COP1, a central integrator of light signaling, senses temperature via an intrinsically disordered region, suggesting how thermomorphogenesis can be modulated according to different climates.

item.title: Cell: Nicotianamine-driven nickel transport to sink organs underpins maize productivity
item.description: A node-phloem-localized nicotianamine efflux transporter in maize regulates Ni delivery to sink organs, including seeds, where Ni-dependent urease activity promotes amino acid metabolism, revealing an unappreciated role of Ni in the yield formation of graminaceous plants.

item.title: Cell: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings
item.description: An scRNA-seq framework that embeds each sample by the density distribution of its cells across cellular states is used to resolve continuous variation in infection, neurodegeneration, embryonic development, and whole-organism perturbation that discrete sample labels obscure.

item.title: Nature: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
Science: Discovering molecular modulators with nanoswitch screening
Science: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression
Science: Targeting hormone conversion through dietary fiber improves polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome
Science: The first 1000 days: Modeling language learning from individual children’s everyday speech
Science: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
Science: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
Science: Direct evidence for psychoactive cannabis use 2800 years ago
Science: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
Science: Denoising the US Census: Succinct block hierarchical regression
Science: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
Science: Echoes of the Anthropocene: Noise pollution as a global threat
Science: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
Nature: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
Cell: CRISPR mutagenesis of the MYC locus reveals a druggable ultraconserved RNA element
item.description: CRISPR tiling mutagenesis of the 10-kb human MYC locus mapped the fitness landscape of an entire human gene at base-pair resolution. This unbiased interrogation revealed that 67% of functionally essential base pairs are noncoding. An ultraconserved RNA regulatory element was identified that controls MYC localization and can be therapeutically targeted to suppress cancer cell growth in patient-derived tumor organoids.

item.title: Nature: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
item.description: A high-throughput CRISPR-interference platform allows the mapping of interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , revealing many previously unknown genetic interactions and providing insight into gene function and drug–target relationships that could enable the development of new therapies for tuberculosis.

item.title: Nature: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
item.description: Gene network analysis shows how mutations in diverse genes associated with autism spectrum disorder can converge to exert shared effects, with X-linked transcription factor ZFX emerging as a key protective factor in the female brain.

item.title: Nature: An open structure-guided RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
item.description: structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence–structure pairs, learns multimodal representations that improve secondary and tertiary structure prediction, functional inference and zero-shot generalization across diverse RNA families.

item.title: Nature: A conserved flowering-time module underlies double-season cropping
item.description: The genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China are traced using representative cultivars, demonstrating how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

item.title: Nature: Microbiome-wide PheWAS links gut microbial SNVs to health and exposures
item.description: Gut microbial single-nucleotide variants across 10,781 individuals reveal 940 associations that link strain-level genetic variation to 69 host traits, with structural analyses pinpointing host phenotype-associated variants, providing a base pair-resolution resource for mechanistic hypothesis generation.

item.title: Nature: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila
item.description: In Drosophila erecta , food odours initiate male sexual arousal, which is subsequently reinforced by the visual motion of other courting flies, creating a multisensory mechanism that synchronizes courtship in groups when conditions are favourable for reproduction.

item.title: Nature: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
item.description: Multi-omic analyses of cells from patients with glioblastoma (GB) provide insight into the role of non-genetic cellular plasticity in disease progression, showing that state stability in GB cells is controlled by a network of interacting activators and repressors.

item.title: Nature: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
item.description: Genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals are analysed, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which alternative archaeological and linguistic models for the origin and spread of Celtic fit reconstructed demographic histories.

item.title: Nature: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
item.description: Aggression experience and observation recruit a brain-wide network of excitatory, inhibitory and valence signals, and changes to this activation pattern predict a shared adaptive behaviour-control policy in a new aggression context.

item.title: Nature: A spatiotemporal cancer cell trajectory underlies glioblastoma heterogeneity
item.description: A deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma is generated, pairing transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling, and tracing glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity to a stereotyped and spatially patterned trajectory of cancer cells.

item.title: Nature: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting
item.description: Codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting is a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells.

item.title: Nature: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
item.description: Longitudinal tracking of endothelial cells shows they can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 and form new functional vessels, challenging conventional views of the essential role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and providing insight into resistance to anti-VEGF therapies.

item.title: Nature: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
item.description: A dopamine pathway to the basolateral amygdala is necessary for associating nutrients with flavours.

item.title: Nature: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells
item.description: Nectin-4 is identified as a pivotal host entry receptor for respiratory transmission and early placental infection of rubella virus.

item.title: Nature: Synergy in viral–bacterial co-infection expedites algal bloom demise
item.description: Viral–bacterial synergy accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality, driven by Alteromonas chemoattraction and co-infection, revealing a previously unrecognized mortality agent that influences oceanic carbon cycling .

item.title: Nature: In vivo CAR-T double knockout screen maps synergistic antitumour gene pairs
item.description: Using high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double knockout screening, synergistic gene combinations to improve CAR-T cell therapy are revealed.

item.title: Nature: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
item.description: The X-ray visualization platform TomoSAXS, demonstrated here on intervertebral spinal discs, can visualize nanoscale to macroscale mechanics in intact biological organs and fibrous materials.

item.title: Cell: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism
item.description: Integration of microbiome omics and host data from globally diverse human populations shows that industrialization restructures gut microbial ecosystems and intestinal physiology. These shifts include reduced microbial diversity, compositional heterogeneity, and community stability; altered intestinal immune and physiological responses; and limited cross-population portability of microbiome-based disease predictors.

item.title: Cell: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient
item.description: Analysis of globally diverse gut bacterial isolate genomes shows that host environments across the industrialization gradient shape genome remodeling and convergent selection, while industrialization is linked to increased HGT-driven gene acquisition and expanded genome size.

item.title: Cell: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury
item.description: We identify a TECR palmitoylation-dependent necrotic cell death (TPNCD) pathway. Blocking TPNCD genetically or pharmacologically protects against immune- and drug-induced liver injury, revealing a therapeutic strategy for hepatic injury.

item.title: Cell: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes
item.description: Ancient DNA data and stable isotope data from the eastern Colombian Andes reveal that C4-enriched resources were incorporated into local food webs during five millennia of genetic continuity and that a later population turnover introduced people with ancestry admixed between that found in Chibchan-related groups and that found at the Amazonian-Andean interface.

item.title: Cell: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis
item.description: Polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism shapes cell fate decisions: loss of DGLA favors senescence, whereas DGLA repletion triggers ferroptosis.

item.title: Cell: Age-dependent structural evolution of a functional amyloid contributes to memory impairment in Drosophila
item.description: In the aging Drosophila brain, Orb2 amyloids required for long-term memory undergo structural remodeling, shifting from translation-promoting assemblies to destabilization-resistant, translation-deficient states. Rebalancing Orb2 toward youthful, translationally active assemblies improves memory in old flies.

item.title: Cell: Genetic coupling of floral rewards and signals underlies pollinator attraction
item.description: Floral rewards and signals must be coordinated to attract pollinators, but the underlying genetic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using melon as a model system, this study reveals how the developmental regulator YAB5 coordinates nectar production, flower opening, and floral signals to promote bee visitation.

item.title: Cell: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication
item.description: Single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary input of viral genomes, which varies with different viruses and cell types. We show that supra-unitary viral genome quantities, independently of viral protein synthesis, activate negative feedback regulators of RIG-I, MDA-5, and PKR, suppressing the innate immune response and allowing replication.

item.title: Cell: Long-range actin-driven endosymbiont mobility in an animal-algal symbiosis
item.description: Hundreds to thousands of dinoflagellate symbionts (Amphidinium sp., 10–20 μm in size) move up to hundreds of micrometers inside the tissue of their acoel worm hosts (Waminoa sp., millimeters in size). Host actin machinery is primarily responsible for driving symbiont mobility at speeds around 1 μm/s, and symbionts move inside ribbon-like host cells (∼200 nm thin), which stretch to accommodate symbionts moving through them.

item.title: Cell: Somatic DNA-repeat expansions initiate distinct yet analogous changes in Huntington’s disease cortical and striatal neurons
item.description: Single-cell-resolution analysis of brain tissue in Huntington's disease (HD) reveals that cortical and striatal neurons pass through analogous biological changes, each initiated by a neuron's own expanding DNA repeat. In cortical neurons, as in striatal neurons, the DNA repeat expands somatically over decades (phases A and B) and becomes toxic at about 150 CAGs, initiating cell-identity erosion (phase C), the formation of nuclear inclusions of aggregated HTT protein, a derepression crisis (phase D), and then death of the neuron.

item.title: Cell: Multimodal spatial transcriptomics redefines cortical pathology in Huntington’s disease
item.description: By using multimodal spatial transcriptomics to measure somatic repeat expansion, huntingtin pathology, and transcriptional profile in every cell of intact tissue sections, we identify in the Huntington’s disease cortex that large somatic CAG repeat expansions are linked to the selective loss of L5–6 NP and L6b deep-layer excitatory neurons. Intranuclear inclusions of huntingtin were most prevalent at intermediate somatic repeat expansions and were associated with broader transcriptional changes than somatic repeat expansion alone.

item.title: Nature: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
item.description: Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits.

item.title: Nature: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
item.description: Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking.

item.title: Nature: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
item.description: Phase 1 of TenK10K takes single-cell RNA sequencing and matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals, enabling detection of associations for common and rare genetic variants, the latter of which have been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression.

item.title: Nature: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature
item.description: Sensorimotor and amygdala activation, but not canonical prefrontal control circuits, indicate emotion regulation capacity.

item.title: Nature: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
item.description: Single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling identifies cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific genetic effects that link non-coding variants to immune disease risk.

item.title: Nature: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
item.description: A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin.

item.title: Nature: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
item.description: Dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory.

item.title: Nature: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics
item.description: Analysis of newly sequenced and previously published ancient human genomes identifies migrations associated with the spread of the Germanic language group, from its arrival in Scandinavia 4,000 years ago, through to its diversification during the historical period.

item.title: Nature: Eukaryotes’ closest relatives are internally simple syntrophic peptidotrophic archaea
item.description: Cultures reveal conservation of cell structure, physical symbioses and anaerobiosis across Heimdallarchaeia (the archaeal lineage that branches closest to eukaryotes) and other Promethearchaeota.

item.title: Nature: Presynaptic homeostasis mediated by exocytosis of a SNARE protein
item.description: Experiments show that when subjected to high-frequency stimulation, excitatory neurons exhibit a presynaptic form of homeostatic plasticity mediated by the exocytosis of v-SNARE protein VAMP7 and the resulting inhibition of P/Q-type calcium channels.

item.title: Nature: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
item.description: A multi-ancestry study of Alzheimer’s disease identifies new risk loci and potential drug targets, implicates microglia and neurons, and reveals a larger common-variant contribution than previously estimated.

item.title: Nature: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
item.description: Pharmacological inhibition of the m 7 G methyltransferase METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and substantially prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin.

item.title: Nature: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
item.description: Loss of function of canonical BAF induces gain of CTCF and cohesin binding that alters 3D genome architecture and reprograms transcription.

item.title: Nature: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
item.description: Single-neuron sequencing shows that widespread genomic abnormalities are common prenatally but largely eliminated around birth, indicating developmental genome quality control in human neurons.

item.title: Nature: Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
item.description: Tumour assembloids, which model components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts and tumour-infiltrating immune cells, are used to identify an essential pathway that mediates heterogeneous therapeutic responses.

item.title: Nature: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism
item.description: In mouse myocardium, glucose oxidation persists in the absence of the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier, with mitochondrial MCT1 importing lactate into mitochondria and LDHB oxidizing it to pyruvate and NADH, sustaining cardiac energetics and preventing stress-induced heart failure.

item.title: Nature: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
item.description: A geoarchaeological survey of the Rub’ al Khali (the Empty Quarter of Arabia) and spatial modelling of the Arabian Peninsula suggest that human settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and stone suitable for making tools, rather than water alone.

item.title: Nature: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
item.description: In systemic lupus erythematosus, aberrant splicing in neutrophils generates novel peptides that are presented on MHC I, driving CD4 + and CD8 + T cell activation, clonal expansion and IgG autoantibody responses, establishing neoantigen-driven autoimmune immunity.

item.title: Cell: Deep sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes uncovers substantial contribution of rare variants to agronomic traits
item.description: Deep coverage sequencing of 3,367 maize genomes reveals substantial contributions of rare variants to trait heritability and provides insights into how selection reshapes their contribution to complex traits.

item.title: Cell: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
item.description: A single-dose AAV-CRISPR therapy restores dystrophin in humanized DMD mice and achieves durable editing with manageable safety in non-human primates. In a first-in-human DMD trial, the therapy yields molecular evidence of muscle editing but reveals a fatal dose-dependent immune complication, highlighting the urgent need to expand the safety margin of systemic AAV-CRISPR treatments.

item.title: Nature: ctDNA clearance and outcomes for resectable lung cancer from NeoCOAST-2
Cell: Perforin triggers iron-induced mitochondrial damage to drive ferroptosis and anti-tumor immunity
item.description: Perforin is best known for delivering granzymes into tumor cells, but this study shows it has a second, independent killing function: it drives iron uptake and mitochondrial iron overload that trigger ferroptosis. This granzyme-independent pathway links cytotoxic immunity to iron metabolism, predicts patient response to checkpoint blockade, and points to iron supplementation as a possible lever for boosting anti-tumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: Taurine lowers inflammaging by regulating the NLRP3 inflammasome in macrophages
item.description: Taurine levels increase with age in mice and humans. Boosting taurine levels even further in aged mice increases health span and dampens inflammation through its regulation of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

item.title: Cell: Cell-state-specific metabolic networks govern ferroptosis versus apoptosis in small cell lung cancer
item.description: SCLC cell states dictate how cancer cells respond to metabolic stress, revealing how metabolic plasticity determines whether the cells undergo ferroptosis or apoptosis.

item.title: Cell: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss
item.description: The orphan transporter MCT6 is the route by which the meal- and exercise-associated metabolite Lac-Phe exits intestinal cells and enters the blood. Mice lacking gut MCT6 cannot maintain normal circulating Lac-Phe levels and exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss, establishing metabolite export as a regulatory node for systemic action.

item.title: Cell: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive
item.description: Single-molecule imaging reveals that metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive, and it relies on the repeated recruitment of Pol α and Pol δ rather than their stable replisome association, thereby uncoupling leading- and lagging-strand synthesis.

item.title: Cell: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade
item.description: Dietary and microbial alterations increase susceptibility to irAEs by promoting IFN-γ-driven Treg fragility and cytotoxic tissue-resident T cell responses. Treg-specific disruption of IFN-γ signaling restores tissue homeostasis and reduces irAEs without compromising antitumor immunity, highlighting Treg stability as a potential therapeutic strategy for limiting checkpoint blockade toxicity.

item.title: Cell: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons
item.description: Computational reconstruction, screening, and engineering of non-LTR retrotransposons uncovers elements, termed Gene Writers, that enable stable transgene integration in human cells using all-RNA delivery. After extensive characterization and optimization, Gene Writers is deployed to generate functional CAR-T cells in vivo in a humanized mouse model.

item.title: Cell: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression
item.description: Selective pharmacological induction of ferroptosis in vivo has remained difficult. By developing the bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor KY0418, this work links systemic ferroptosis induction to tissue metabolic remodeling and demonstrates context-dependent suppression of tumor progression, including metastatic spread.

item.title: Cell: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula
item.description: Roman and post-Roman Iberia was transformed by extensive mobility across the Mediterranean, with large-scale inputs from Eastern Mediterranean and North African populations reshaping its genetic landscape. During the migration period, Central-Northern European ancestry arrived largely through elite-associated groups that intermarried with local populations but did not replace the highly diverse population that had formed under Roman rule.

item.title: Cell: Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse
item.description: A multi-omic atlas of human T cell exhaustion reveals that dysfunctional T cells undergo broad remodeling of protein turnover and ubiquitin regulation that is not captured by transcriptomic analysis. The E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF166 regulates T cell persistence and anti-tumor function, highlighting proteostasis as a targetable axis for improving immunotherapy.

item.title: Nature: The anatomy of a personal health agent
item.description: A multi-agent framework that coordinates data science, medical reasoning and health coaching over longitudinal wearable and clinical data to provide holistic personal health support is described.

item.title: Cell: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females
item.description: isoUDCA, a female-enriched bile acid produced by a gut bacterial consortium favored by estrogen, promotes hepatic cholesterol handling and bile acid metabolism through SREBP2-STARD4-CYP7B1 signaling, thereby alleviating chronic liver injury.

item.title: Cell: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion
item.description: ʟ-Carnitine is a nonproteinogenic amino acid highly abundant in myocytes, and both excess ingestion of myocytes and myocyte necrosis are associated with systemic inflammation. Here, we find that the pyrin inflammasome senses extracellular ʟ-carnitine through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and this leads to IL-1β-mediated inflammation. Our findings position OCTN2 as a potential target to reduce inflammation from exogenous or endogenous sources of extracellular ʟ-carnitine.

item.title: Cell: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
item.description: A 22-tissue multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise is generated, detailing tissue-, sex-, and time-dependent molecular adaptations and cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling in skeletal muscle. The atlas reveals coordinated transcriptomic, epigenetic, proteomic, and metabolic remodeling across the body.

item.title: Cell: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
item.description: Coleoid cephalopods edit their RNA at a level far beyond other animals, but the functional consequences to the proteome have been largely unknown. Proteomic detection of recoded sites reveals that single amino acid edits alter protein stability, subcellular localization, post-translational modification, and organelle function.

item.title: Cell: An opioid efficacy switch for reversible optical control of analgesia
item.description: Azo-morphine-3 (AM-3) is a photoswitchable ligand that toggles between low and high efficacy states to control mu-opioid receptor activity in vitro and in vivo both in the brain and periphery. AM-3 provides a powerful tool to probe the structural basis of opioid efficacy and enables spatiotemporally precise control of analgesia across pain models with reduced side effects compared with systemic drugs.

item.title: Cell: Cellular self-organization orchestrates ferroptosis propagation
item.description: Local cell-cell interactions give rise to emergent cellular patterns that encode ferroptosis-sensitive and -resistant fates and establish polarized lipid organization within cells. These coupled biochemical and biophysical properties enable self-organized cell populations to orient and confine otherwise isotropic, unbounded ferroptosis propagation, revealing a systems-level mechanism that regulates collective cell fate.

item.title: Cell: Mitochondria-targeted tetraoxanes initiate lipid peroxidation to drive ferroptosis and tumor suppression
item.description: Pan et al. report tetraoxane-containing compounds WMK-1/2 as first-generation mitochondrial lipid peroxidation inducers that bypass GPX4- and retinol-mediated defenses to trigger a distinct “mito-ferroptosis” sub-pathway, demonstrating potent bioavailable tumor-suppressive activity across multiple in vivo models.

item.title: Cell: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
item.description: By studying nearly half a million human genomes, this work shows that structural variants, large changes in DNA sequence greater than 50 base pairs, are an important and previously underrecognized source of human disease risk. The resulting resource reveals rare and regulatory structural variants linked to disease, providing insights into human biology and accelerating the development of medicines.

item.title: Cell: A pseudoenzyme sensor of trehalose-6-phosphate directly represses the metabolic integrator SnRK1 in plants
item.description: In Arabidopsis, pseudoenzyme class II T6P synthase functions as a T6P sensor that directly represses the master metabolic regulator SnRK1, highlighting a conserved switch that couples carbon availability to metabolic homeostasis in plants.

item.title: Nature: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
item.description: Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.

item.title: Nature: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
item.description: A tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells.

item.title: Nature: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation
item.description: Primary cultured haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are used to analyse the molecular mechanisms of brain myeloid differentiation, and this platform enabled the identification of elongation factor ELP1 as an important regulator of this process.

item.title: Nature: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
item.description: Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

item.title: Nature: Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
item.description: A randomized controlled trial involving a health-education intervention in rural villages in Honduras shows that the intervention changed social network connections, including not only health-related connections but also friendships and financial ties.

item.title: Cell: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
item.description: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

item.title: Cell: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
item.description: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

item.title: Cell: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
item.description: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

item.title: Cell: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
item.description: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

item.title: Cell: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting
item.description: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that infers causal regulators from single-cell experiments by mapping their transcriptional responses onto reference perturbation dictionaries.

item.title: Nature: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception
item.description: An effector regulatory T cell circuit is identified that can be monitored in blood samples to track the development of lung cancer, and blockade of this immune network in the preinvasive setting can intercept tumorigenesis to reduce tumour incidence and size.

item.title: Nature: tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer
item.description: A tRNA-specific regulatory pathway is associated with codon biology, lineage transitions and therapy resistance in prostate cancer.

item.title: Nature: A gut microbial odd-chain fatty acid alleviates atherosclerosis in mice
item.description: The administration of Bacteroides uniformis in mice can mitigate atherosclerosis via pentadecanoic acid, which directly inhibits HMG-CoA reductase to promote hepatic cholesterol clearance.

item.title: Cell: A non-canonical function of glutathione to suppress ferroptosis via FSP1
item.description: Glutathione (GSH) robustly defends against ferroptosis independently of GPX4. FSP1 utilizes GSH to reduce ubiquinone and subsequently inhibits ferroptosis, which is distinct from the NAD(P)H-FAD axis. Targeting the FSP1-GSH axis efficiently alleviated ferroptosis-induced tissue injury.

item.title: Cell: A spatiotemporal lifecycle atlas decodes spatial coordination in rice
item.description: A 3D spatiotemporal cell atlas of rice spanning the entire seed-to-seed lifecycle. Developmental trajectories are captured, and the spatially distinct roles of OsARF1 in rice development and dorsoventral endosperm asymmetry related to starch and protein accumulation are revealed.

item.title: Cell: SPARCS enables scalable recovery of complex image-based phenotypes for genetic screening
item.description: Current genetic screens face a trade-off between scaling to large mutant libraries and measuring information-rich phenotypes. SPARCS automates laser microdissection to enable pooled forward genetic screens for complex image-based phenotypes at scale. By physically recovering individual mutants, SPARCS supports multimodal profiling of hits beyond genotyping, including via mass spectrometry-based proteomics.

item.title: Cell: Cancer competition for vitamin B2 creates metabolic checkpoint for T cell ferroptosis
item.description: A CRISPR screen of solute carriers reveals that T cells depend on SLC52A3 for VB2 uptake, whereas tumors preferentially exploit SLC52A2 to outcompete them, thereby driving T cell ferroptosis. Enforced SLC52A3 overexpression in T cells reverses this metabolic competition and enhances their antitumor activity.

item.title: Cell: Salicylic acid engages central metabolic regulators SnRK1 and TOR to govern immunity by differential phosphorylation of NPR1
item.description: The immune signal SA triggers metabolic changes to activate SnRK1 while inhibiting TOR. These central metabolic kinases antagonistically phosphorylate the key immune regulator NPR1, thereby coupling cellular metabolic state to systemic acquired resistance.

item.title: Cell: Gut microbiota primes stroke severity via the AHR in intestinal dendritic cells
item.description: Indole-producing Escherichia coli worsens ischemic stroke through the activation of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in dendritic cells. Limiting AHR signaling in DCs promotes gut-derived DC migration to the meninges, expands meningeal regulatory T cells, and reduces neuroinflammation. This microbiota-AHR axis offers a promising therapeutic target.

item.title: Cell: Spatial evolution of a cachexia-promoting microenvironment in pancreatic cancer
item.description: Pancreatic cancer cachexia is accompanied by progressive assembly of a spatially organized tumor-macrophage-fibroblast niche. Reciprocal signaling among the cellular populations in the niche is associated with muscle wasting and cachexia progression.

item.title: Cell: Microbiome signatures linked to cancer and treatment adverse events in a real-world cohort
item.description: In a large, real-world mixed-cancer cohort, analyses accounting for comorbidities and additional confounders indicate that most microbiome alterations are shared across cancers rather than specific to individual cancers. Distinct associations are limited to a subset of cancers and, in separate analyses, to age of onset and specific treatment-related adverse events.

item.title: Cell: Cargo crosslinking nucleates AP-1 lattice formation
item.description: Cargo has traditionally been viewed as a passive substrate of coat-mediated transport. Cryo-EM reveals that cargo containing tandem sorting motifs directly promotes higher-order adaptor assembly by bridging AP-1 complexes, enabling efficient trafficking and neuronal development in zebrafish.

item.title: Cell: Non-invasive control of gene editing in vivo by photoswitchable Cas12f and focused ultrasound
item.description: Remote activation of a single-AAV-deliverable photoswitchable Cas12f system enables precise spatial and temporal control of genome editing in deep tissues without surgery or implanted devices.

item.title: Cell: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex
item.description: In-cell cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) combined with proteomics, integrative structural modeling, and bioinformatics enables discovery and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins. In the minimal bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae, this reveals a complex that links Sec-based protein translocation and extracellular folding, capable of supporting both co- and post-translational pathways.

item.title: Cell: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries
item.description: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) resolves and quantifies an almost complete view of bacterial translation, revealing how gene expression machineries coordinate across the processes of transcription, translation, and membrane engagement directly within a minimal bacterium.

item.title: Cell: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration
item.description: APOE4 causes a pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition that promotes cerebrovascular fibrosis and perivascular amyloid accumulation. TGF-β inhibition reverses this pathological remodeling and thus presents a therapeutic strategy to restore cerebrovascular homeostasis in these high-risk individuals.

item.title: Cell: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation
item.description: Mammalian embryos see a substantial increase in available oxygen once the placenta forms. This increase in oxygen exposure serves as a trigger for initiating the development of the hindlimb, thus controlling developmental timing and, more broadly, linking the maternal environment to evolutionary changes in body plan.

item.title: Cell: Microbial signaling coordinates group oviposition and predator defense in migratory locusts
item.description: This study reveals an egg-associated bacterial signaling mechanism that couples reproductive synchronization with offspring defense in the locust L. migratoria, expanding the functional landscape of insect-microbe-predator interactions and demonstrating how microbial signals can shape complex ecological behaviors.

item.title: Cell: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
item.description: Retrotransposons can infect neighboring cells using a mechanism that relies on a small fusogen-like protein rather than on the envelope protein that is typically required for infection.

item.title: Cell: Projection-defined modules reveal mouse motor cortex architecture
item.description: The mouse motor cortex divides into 16 spatially organized modules based on distinct subcortical projections. This specificity covaries with cortical connectivity patterns and cell-type composition along two spatial axes, thereby defining the rules by which motor cortex modules integrate with granularity into brainwide and precisely wired neuronal networks to influence movement.

item.title: Cell: CD4 T cells convert transient responses to KRAS inhibition to durable remissions in pancreatic cancer
item.description: An AI-designed IL-21 mimetic converts transient KRAS inhibitor responses into durable pancreatic cancer remissions through CD4 T cells, independent of CD8 T cells and tumor MHC class I expression.

item.title: Cell: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway
item.description: Cold-stress signals are transmitted to chloroplasts and subsequently trigger cold responses through an RAF-like bi-kinase module where cytoplasmic RAF3 and plasma membrane RAF6 translocate to chloroplasts, where they inhibit photosynthetic activity but activate nuclear cold-responsive gene expression.

item.title: Cell: mRNA-encoding CD19-targeting T cell engager for refractory immune thrombocytopenia
item.description: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle-encoded CD19×CD3 T cell engager depletes B cells with attenuated cytokine release in preclinical models. In three patients with treatment-refractory immune thrombocytopenia, treatment with this T cell engager achieved sustained platelet recovery over 6 months, suggesting that mRNA-encoded T cell engagers represent a promising therapeutic approach for resetting autoreactive immunity in B cell-driven autoimmune disease.

item.title: Cell: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery
item.description: Phosphorothioates, stereospecific modifications of the RNA phosphate backbone in anaerobic archaea, expand the epitranscriptome beyond nucleobases and ribose sugars. Installed by Esti enzymes at conserved rRNA and tRNA hotspots, these environmentally responsive marks stabilize tRNAs and support growth at high temperatures.

item.title: Cell: 3D chromatin remodeling during domestication defines novel targets for crop improvement
item.description: Population-level 3D genome atlas of 34 semi-wild and 267 cultivated allotetraploid cottons reveals domestication-selected chromatin conformations that enhance cotton fiber quality and unlock cryptic breeding targets.

item.title: Cell: Gliomas phenocopy an inborn error of metabolism to drive neuronal activity and tumor growth
item.description: Glioma-derived guanidinoacetate depolarizes neighboring neurons through γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) A receptors, and depleting this metabolite reduces both neuronal activity and glioma growth.

item.title: Cell: Single-cell-resolved genome atlas of prokaryoplankton inhabiting the ocean’s interior
item.description: GORG-Dark presents genomes of 9,698 individual bacterial and archaeal cells from the ocean’s sunless interior. The atlas resolves depth stratification to abyssal waters, uncovers particle-attached Pelagibacterales, maps chemolithoautotrophy and biosynthetic gene clusters, and identifies a rhodopsin clade specific to the dark ocean.

item.title: Cell: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting triggers translational stress to promote viral replication
item.description: Viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 can use programmed ribosomal frameshifting to turn off host translation and promote viral replication, expanding the known uses of programmed ribosomal frameshifting by viruses.

item.title: Cell: Norway spruce spatiotemporal programs of conifer reproductive development
item.description: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics across conifer reproductive and vegetative shoots reveals candidate developmental regulators and evolutionarily conserved tissue patterning genes in seed plants.

item.title: Cell: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
item.description: Cell-mediated immunity requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Here, D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) is shown to act as a metabolic adjuvant, driving the conversion of proliferating CD8+ T cells into cytotoxic effector cells by linking mitochondrial ATP production to chromatin remodeling and gene expression.

item.title: Cell: Architecture of the serotonergic projectome in the mouse brain
item.description: Serotonin neurons innervate nearly the entire mammalian brain, yet how their projections are organized has remained unclear. Systematic whole-brain serotonergic axon collateralization mapping reveals five projectomic groups that preferentially target functionally related regions, with each projectomic group connecting to specific spatial transcriptomic and behavioral profiles.

item.title: Cell: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host
item.description: How do maternal gut bacteria seed the rapidly developing neonatal gut? Heo et al. show that Bacteroides fragilis produces a distinct membrane lipid that enables this strict anaerobe to tolerate a microaerobic environment. This finding highlights divergent evolutionary strategies among related species, most of which rely on lipids conferring broader fitness.
